name: Texture streaming and mipmaps
title: 텍스처 스트리밍
summary: Texture streaming and mipmaps manage texture memory allocation in real-time by dynamically loading lower-resolution texture maps based on camera distance, preventing VRAM overflow.
when: Large open-world games where millions of square units of textured terrain and buildings are rendered simultaneously
Projects targeting platforms with limited VRAM such as mobile devices or older graphics cards
Optimizing overall performance to prevent hitching and out-of-memory crashes during high-speed camera movement
steps: Open the Unreal Engine project and navigate to the Content Browser where target textures are located.
Double-click a texture asset to open the Texture Editor window and inspect current compression and streaming settings.
In the Details panel under Level of Detail, verify that 'Mip Gen Settings' is set to 'FromTextureGroup' or 'NoMipmaps' depending on usage.
Adjust 'Texture Group' in the Details panel to categorize the texture (e.g., World, Character, UI) for global streaming pool management.
Check 'Never Stream' if the texture must remain fully loaded in memory at all times, such as UI elements or critical mask maps.
Save the texture asset and verify that VRAM usage updates accordingly in the viewport statistics.

params.name: Mip Gen Settings
params.desc: Determines how lower-resolution mipmap levels are automatically generated for the texture.

params.name: Texture Group
params.desc: Assigns the texture to a specific group for collective resolution scaling and streaming control.

params.name: Never Stream
params.desc: Forces the texture to stay fully loaded in memory, disabling streaming behavior for this asset.

params.name: LOD Bias
params.desc: Shifts the texture mipmap selection to lower resolutions to save VRAM at the cost of sharpness.

params.name: Max Texture Size
params.desc: Caps the maximum resolution of the texture loaded into memory regardless of the source file.

examples.title: Optimizing a massive landscape terrain texture
steps: Select the giant landscape base color texture in the Content Browser.
Set 'Texture Group' to 'World' in the Details panel to apply standard terrain streaming rules.
Ensure mipmaps are enabled so distant landscape tiles load smaller resolutions automatically.

examples.title: Preventing texture blur on a close-up cinematic hero prop
steps: Locate the primary hero prop texture in the Content Browser.
Open the Details panel and check the 'Never Stream' option to lock full resolution in memory.
Adjust 'Max Texture Size' to allow 4K or 8K resolution without reduction.

mistakes: Textures appearing blurry when viewed up close → Increase texture streaming pool size or check if 'Never Stream' is needed for critical assets.
VRAM exceeding limits in large scenes → Enable mipmaps on all world textures and assign correct Texture Groups.
